title_as_printed: Partial Molar Volumes of Sodium Chloride Solutions at 200 bar, and Temperatures from 175 to 350 C
experimental_method: Mercury displacement technique: solution in a stainless-steel vessel in a molten-salt bath, expansion at constant 200 bar measured by weighing mercury bled off, converted to density.
uncertainties_stated: Temperature accurate to 0.01 C; volume calibration 0.01 cm3 (~10 ppm); uncertainty of apparent molar volume tabulated in Table II (5.6 to 57.0 cm3/mol at m=0.1, 0.14 to 1.5 at m=4.0); density uncertainty from 0.01 C temperature error 6e-5; reference densities about 30 ppm above Vaslow-based values.
quality_remarks: Possible hydrogen from corrosion of unlined vessel judged negligible by authors (no pressure drift). The m=2.0 isopleth consists of three runs; apparent molar volume smooth within 1.0 cm3/mol. Agreement with Hilbert 0.1%.
not_extracted_tables: Table II: uncertainties of apparent molar volume (derived)
Table III: standard partial molar volumes (derived by extrapolation, includes literature rows)
